business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Channel Omni-Helpdesk and Conversational Bot Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal Confederation level; cantonal commercial register offices act as executive registrars under federal law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental Roman-Germanic doctrine) based on codified federal statutes and the Swiss Civil Code (SR 210) and Code of Obligations (SR 220); no binding judicial precedent doctrine (Federal Supreme Court decisions are persuasive only); federal law prevails over cantonal law and is directly applicable
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Sino-Swiss Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 3 February 1986, in force)
Swiss-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income (1951, as amended by the 1996 protocol and the 2009 protocol)
Sino-Swiss Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (signed 25 September 2013, in force from 4 January 2014)
Bilateral Agreements I between Switzerland and the European Union (including the Agreement on Free Movement of Persons of 21 June 1999 and the 1972 Free Trade Agreement)
EFTA Convention (1960) and Switzerland's network of over 30 free trade agreements applicable to service industries
New York Convention (1958) and ICSID Convention applicable through Swiss private international law (SR 291) for investor-state arbitration

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA/GwG; SR 955.0) as amended, with the Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO; SR 955.01); Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0) Arts. 305bis and 305ter; Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 626-640, 958-963 and 697j; Federal Commercial Register Ordinance (ORV; SR 221.411) and Name Ordinance (SR 221.413.1); Federal Act on the Protection of Swiss Public Coats of Arms and other Signs (SR 232.21); Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Transparency Act) implementing Art. 98a of the Federal Constitution after the 3 March 2024 popular vote and establishing an authority-accessible beneficial ownership register with expected entry into force in 2026; FINMA Circulars 2020/1 (AML due diligence) and 2011/01 (audit and governance) applicable as regulatory guidance
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the future Transparency Act register and the underlying shareholder/debenture-holder register of the AG are not publicly accessible; only FINMA, MROS, tax, commercial-register authorities and licensed gatekeepers such as notaries, fiduciaries and banks obtain UBO data; the shareholder register of an AG with nominal shares remains private; bearer shares are subject to mandatory registration and custody rules under Art. 697i-697m OR)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the current passport or national ID of each natural-person founder, director, authorized signatory and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil registration authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (1961) applied by the competent authority of the issuing country; for non-Apostille states, Swiss consular legalization at the competent Swiss embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the commercial/company register and certificate of good standing of any corporate founder or corporate UBO (e.g., corporate excerpt of a PRC company or foreign-registered entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign commercial register authority (e.g., PRC Administration for Market Regulation as banking certificate extract; ACRA in Singapore; Companies House in the United Kingdom)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (1961) or consular legalization, followed by a certified German, French or Italian translation (or certified English where the register accepts English)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft/stock corporation), art. 621 (minimum capital CHF 100,000), art. 632 para. 2 (minimum paid-up capital), art. 640 (registration in the Commercial Register), art. 643 (registered office and purpose), art. 626 (articles of association), art. 727a (audit opt-out); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), arts. 2-20; Cantonal Notarial Act of the Canton of Zug.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), acting under the legal supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Secretariat (Handelsregisterfachstelle) of the Swiss Federal Office of Justice (FOJ)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarially certified deed of incorporation (Errichtungsakt) containing the Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts), together with the official Commercial Register application form (Anmeldung) and the bank's confirmation of paid-up capital, submitted through the Canton of Zug electronic commercial register portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital CHF 100,000 (OR art. 621). At incorporation, at least 20% of the par value of each share must be paid in cash and the aggregate paid-in amount must reach at least CHF 50,000 (OR art. 632 para. 2). The paid-up capital must be deposited on a blocked bank account in the company's name (escrow arrangement) and is released only after registration; contributions in kind require an audited formation report by a sworn Swiss auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural constitutive meeting of the Board held at the registered office in Zug, the founding shareholder, having subscribed 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000 par value, is acknowledged. The Board confirms that one half of the nominal capital (CHF 50,000) has been paid on the company's blocked bank account, adopts the registered domicile at [Street], CH-6300 Zug, and appoints [Name] as Chair with individual signing power, [Name] as CEO with individual signing power, and [Name] as Money-Laundering/Data-Protection Compliance Officer. The Board waives the ordinary statutory audit pursuant to art. 727a CO and instructs the CEO to submit the commercial register filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and statutory constitution drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public authorized in the Canton of Zug, with pre-clearance coordination with the Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a company name availability search in the Swiss trademark database and against the Commercial Register index, determine the competence of the registered office (Sitz) in the municipality of Zug, select the nominal capital structure and the share categories, and draft the Articles of Association satisfying OR art. 626 and art. 643. Where the sole shareholder is an individual, prepare the founder's subscription statement and preliminary director consents.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (name, registered office, purpose, capital, share classes, board provisions, audit opt-out)
Company name search result from the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property
Founding shareholder instruction letter and capital allocation plan
Copies of passports and social insurance numbers of all intended directors and authorised signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry pre-check indicates that the proposed name is misleading, unavailable, or conflicts with an existing trademark, amend the name suffix and resubmit the draft for another pre-check; no additional government fee is charged, but notarial drafting costs may increase.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public notarization of the deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the Canton of Zug acting under the Cantonal Notarial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the constitutive meeting of the founders; the notary authenticates the signatures of all subscribing shareholders, certifies the final text of the Articles of Association, verifies the identity and capacity of the directors and records the subscription and payment modality in the public deed. The deed is the core document for the subsequent Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Association in German or French, notarially signed by all shareholders
Notarial deed of incorporation (Errichtungsakt)
Identity certificates of the founders and beneficial owners (AMLA art. 4 declaration)
Authorisation of any corporate subscriber with extract of the official register of its legal form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because a foreign shareholder's signature lacks legalization or apostille, obtain a certified signature through the competent Swiss representation and submit the authenticated copy; the notary then proceeds without modifying the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital payment and blocked account certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank licensed by FINMA, capable of issuing a blocked-account capital certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the company with the bank's Anti-Money-Laundering onboarding. Transfer the minimum paid-in amount of CHF 50,000 exclusively as capital contribution. Instruct the bank to irrevocably block the funds in favour of the company until the Commercial Register registration and to issue the formal paid-up capital certificate (Barzahlungsbescheinigung) in the name of the company and the notary.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association
Draft deed of incorporation
Beneficial owner declaration under AMLA art. 4
KYC documents of all shareholders and signatories
Bank blocked-account confirmation and paid-in capital certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays the blocked-account certificate due to internal KYC review, provide the ownership chart and corporate purpose summary and, where necessary, request the notary to issue a reserve confirmation; the Commercial Register accepts the notary-transmitted bank certificate as controlling documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register application, registration decree, and legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), with publication by the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Commercial Register application form accompanied by the notarial deed, the paid-up capital certificate, duly signed director consents and specimen signatures. The registry examines statutory completeness and legal conformity, issues the registration decree (Eintragungsverfuegung), and causes the entry to be published in SHAB. The company acquires legal personality on registration (OR art. 643); all founders' liability becomes subject to the corporate veil.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register application form for an AG
Notarially certified deed of incorporation including Articles of Association
Bank certificate evidencing payment of CHF 50,000 on a blocked account
Signed consents of the Board of Directors and specimen signatures
Beneficial owner declaration if requested by the registry
Receipt of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an interlocutory query, cure the identified defects (missing purpose clause, incorrect capital statement, or absence of a director consent) within 10 business days by supplementary notarial declaration. If a rejection order is issued, an appeal to the cantonal commercial register review authority may be lodged within 30 days; alternatively, a corrected filing may be resubmitted as a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social insurance, and data protection notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug, Federal Tax Administration (FTA), compensation office for OASI/AVS, SUVA, and Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Register extract, open the corporate tax file with the Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug, apply for a value-added tax number with the FTA if taxable turnover will exceed CHF 250,000 per year or to exercise the option for voluntary VAT, register as an employer with the Federal Social Insurance compensation office and SUVA for workplace accident insurance, and adopt a joint processing register or privacy statement as required under the revised Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP).
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming legal personality
Articles of Association and board resolution on authorised signatories
Founder and director personal identification and tax details
Payroll and social insurance registration form for the first employees
Privacy notice and processing register for customer support data operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration issues a late-application reminder, submit the missing commercial register extract and board resolution immediately; penalties are generally waived where no tax liability was hidden and the good-faith start-up registration occurred within 30 days of the Commercial Register decree.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sectoral industrial licensing institution applies to ISIC 6201 helpdesk and SaaS activities in Switzerland. For physical office operations, the authorities concerned are the Cantonal Fire Inspectorate of Zug (Feuerpolizei), the Municipal Building Inspectorate (Bauinspektorat), the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate, and SUVA for occupational health and safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swiss law does not provide an operating license for helpdesk/cloud software businesses; the only administrative clearances relevant to the rented office premises are the Certificate of Occupancy (Benutzungsbewilligung) issued by the municipality and the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (Brandschutzkontrolle) issued by the Feuerpolizei.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt fuer Umwelt, BAFU/FOEN), acting in coordination with the Amt fuer Umweltschutz des Kantons Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: office-only helpdesk and cloud platform activity without manufacturing plant, warehouse, or fixed installation; no Environmental Impact Assessment (UVP/EIA) is required under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/VO EIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources are installed; office wastewater is discharged through the municipal sewer system under the Federal Water Protection Act (GSchG) without a separate discharge permit; e-waste and end-of-life IT hardware must be routed through certified Swiss take-back schemes (SENS/SWICO) in accordance with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA); any heating or emergency power installations, if present, are subject to the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV) thresholds for CO and NOx.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Feuerpolizei of the Canton of Zug covering escape routes, extinguishing equipment, signage, and alarm systems; structural load clearance of the leased office floor issued by the Municipal Building Inspectorate; and the employer's workplace-safety notification to SUVA complying with the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG) and Ordinance on Safety at Work (VAM), including electrical installation inspections and ergonomic workstation assessments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA) / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) / Administration fédérale des contributions (AFC); official portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities not established in Switzerland but exceeding the VAT threshold must apply for a Swiss Value Added Tax number (MWST-Nummer) via the FTA's electronic VAT registration portal. Entities already entered in the Swiss commercial register receive a Business Identification Number (UID) from the Central Business Name Index (Zefix). The application requires identification documents, proof of business seat or service address, description of activities, turnover estimates, and, if applicable, a Swiss fiscal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: VAT group taxation election under Art. 52 of the Swiss VAT Act for closely linked persons/entities; election for taxation of foreign entities with Swiss permanent establishment; retrospective VAT registration election within 30 days of exceeding threshold; no US-style check-the-box pass-through election under Swiss federal tax law; hybrid mismatch elections limited to specific OECD BEPS-aligned rules for transparent entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 annual worldwide turnover (effective 1 January 2025; previously CHF 100,000, with special registration obligation for non-resident businesses supplying digital services in Switzerland).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax authority API validation, or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is permitted under Swiss eBill/QR-bill standards, and paper or PDF invoices are accepted. VAT invoices must contain prescribed mandatory fields including Swiss VAT identification number, supplier/buyer name and address, date, description, consideration, and applicable rate. Continuous transaction controls are not implemented; periodic VAT returns are filed electronically via the FTA portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Art. 53 of the Swiss VAT Act applies to exported goods, international transport services, and certain cross-border services where the recipient's place of business is abroad. For exported goods, the supplier must provide proof of export by Swiss customs declaration and commercial documentation. For services, zero-rating applies if the recipient is situated outside Switzerland and the service qualifies as B2B cross-border supply; low-value goods and certain e-commerce supplies are subject to specific rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss customs export declaration / Ausfuhrdeklaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank Payment Confirmation
Proof of Physical Exit or Foreign Recipient Business Status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss tax law imposes fines up to CHF 10,000 for tax irregularities, and imprisonment for intentional tax evasion or fraudulent documentation. In case of incorrect zero-rating claims, the FTA may retrospectively assess the VAT due plus interest and claim refunds of input VAT incorrectly credited. The statutory limitation period for tax evasion is 10 years for deliberate concealment, while ordinary assessment periods are 5 years. Swiss courts may also impose penalties for forged customs declarations and export evidence. No specific FX repatriation deadline exists under Swiss VAT law; the 180-day benchmark reflects treasury and anti-money laundering documentation expectations but is not a statutory VAT condition.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) together with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) for banking and AML oversight; the Foreign Exchange Act is not a separate instrument, as Switzerland maintains a liberal free-market FX regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland has full current- and capital-account convertibility under Article 3 of the Swiss Federal Constitution's economic freedom principles and the Foreign Investment and Business Residence regime. The Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible without exchange controls or mandatory approval. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and liquidation proceeds can be transferred abroad without FX approval, subject only to withholding tax on dividends (35% federal, reduced under treaty) and to standard bank KYC/source-of-funds checks. No capital controls, no surrender requirements, and no FX licensing thresholds apply to inbound or outbound payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Switzerland. Swiss exporters may retain proceeds in any currency, convert them freely, or maintain multi-currency accounts with a Swiss bank. The SNB only publishes balance-of-payments statistics based on domestic bank reports; individual companies are not required to surrender export receipts or obtain approval for conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (a UBS Group company / post-integration legal entity)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (electronic money institutions) are not directly passportable into Switzerland. FINMA does not issue EMI licences; foreign digital banks may only offer services to Swiss clients via a licensed Swiss bank/fintech subsidiary (FINMA Fintech Licence per Article 1b Banking Act) or through a strictly inbound Agent Model. Feasibility for using an offshore EMI as primary operating account is Low; it is viable only as a secondary receivables/settlement rail when funds are routed onward to a licensed Swiss bank. Legal constraints require that clients' custody funds and payment services be provided by a FINMA-regulated institution; otherwise the cross-border service may constitute unlicensed banking under Article 1 Banking Act.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not legally required to appear physically at the bank for onboarding. Swiss Financial Market Infrastructure Act and AMLA-compliant remote onboarding via audio-visual video call combined with qualified electronic identification (FinID, SwissID, eID+) is accepted by major banks. A physical visit may be required for accounts with higher-risk profiles, non-EU/EEA shareholders, or complex beneficial-ownership structures. For the target low-risk Helpdesk SaaS entity, remote opening with a Swiss qualified director interview is practically viable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner differs from the nominal shareholder or is located in a high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized share register, Swiss CHF capital deposit confirmation, original/legalized corporate documents, sworn declaration of beneficial ownership, and a clean source-of-funds narrative with audited statements or certificate of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume cross-border transactions from SaaS subscriptions with multiple counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business model explanation, privacy/data-processing contract portfolio, ISAE 3402 / SOC 2 report, IP ownership certificate, three years of billing forecast per country, and AML due-diligence profile of major subscription counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Share capital injected via third-party/offshore payments rather than from a Swiss licensed bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Origin-of-funds declaration from the payor bank, supporting SWIFT MT103 copies, signed board resolution approving capital contribution, verification of source of funds through payroll, dividends, or validated disposal of digital assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of fungible tokens or crypto custody for treasury operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINMA-compliant crypto custody arrangement documented via a licensed Swiss digital asset bank, audited wallet records, and a clear statement that business operations do not involve asset tokens regulated under banking law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfers for share capital injection and non-resident shareholder loans use SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank) with purpose codes to distinguish equity contribution (ISIC 6201; customs tariff unrelated; purpose code 'Capital import – direct investment', Switzerland has no dedicated FX code requirement). The bank requires a board resolution approving the capital increase, proof of deposit at a licensed Swiss bank to remove stamp duty risk (capital issuance above par triggers 1% Stamp Tax), and a source-of-funds dossier. Dividend/interest repatriation requires a W-8/W-9-like Swiss form and, if treaty relief available, a Swiss withholding-tax refund under double-taxation treaty.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for outsourced helpdesk services and software licensing are made through SWIFT MT103/MT202, SEPA EUR transfers, or, for high-value transactions, commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) where the counterparty requires payment guarantees. For recurring SaaS subscriptions, SWIFT MT103 with standard purpose code 'Intellectual property royalties' or 'Information technology services' is used; the bank may request an invoice and a contract extract for reconciliation. Cross-border disbursements from the Swiss account require no exchange-control approval; liquidity is maintained via multi-currency accounts (CHF, EUR, USD) at UBS/ZKB to net incoming and outgoing positions and reduce FX conversion spreads.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency liabilities
Currency options (European-style) on fully convertible major currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only where the reference currency is not freely convertible (e.g., RMB/CNH) and the hedge is documented as a commercial hedge of operating exposure
Overnight indexed swaps and currency basis swaps with a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax on net profit after tax (plus cantonal and municipal profit taxes; combined statutory rate typically 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general federal tax holiday for corporate income. Eligible deductions include participation relief (95% exemption on qualifying dividend income), R&D additional deduction (up to 150% in several cantons, subject to cantonal law), patent box regime for IP-derived income, and equity interest deduction (currently available in certain cantons; subject to OECD transitional rules). A Helpdesk SaaS business may benefit from R&D deductions if software development qualifies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate tax return is filed combined for federal, cantonal and communal taxes using the official 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen' (Form AG/SAR, e.g., Form 720/180 for the Canton of Zug). Electronic filing is mandatory in most cantons via the cantonal tax administration e-portal (e.g., 'TaxWare', 'Ordix' or canton-specific systems) and via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's e-tax interface.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return for a calendar-year-ended AG must be filed within 6 months following the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by 30 June of the following year for most taxpayers). Cantonal authorities may grant extensions of 2 to 6 months upon written request with justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net taxable profit after adjustments shown in the financial statements. This includes intercompany recharge may require arm's length adjustments for helpdesk and support services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Swiss AG owned by non-residents, report only the Swiss enterprise's worldwide profit attributable to the AG; include related-party income at arm's length; no remission to foreign head-office unless a permanent establishment exists in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report net equity (share capital, reserves, retained earnings) as of the balance sheet date. This is used to compute the cantonal equity tax and federal capital contribution confirmation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure subscribed capital is fully paid and documented; share premium and capital contributions are recorded to avoid future dividend disguised as repayment of capital.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State qualifying dividends from domestic and foreign subsidiaries. Apply the participation relief if holding at least 10% for at least one year; 95% of such income is exempt from direct federal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders should have the Swiss AG claim treaty benefits through Form 823 / TD DS 04574; withholding tax reclaim or reduced rate is applied only upon receipt of a tax residency certificate from the foreign jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4 — Direct Federal Tax Rate Adjustment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the statutory net profit to the taxable base after adding back non-deductible expenses (e.g., political donations, excessive director fees, undeducted VAT input).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners' management fees, interest or royalties are deductible in Switzerland only if supported by transfer pricing documentation and arm's length conditions; otherwise the add-back triggers additional withholding tax liabilities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the realized tax loss carryforward to be offset against current profit, capped at 100% of taxable profit but subject to the 7-year statutory limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may only be offset if the proof of loss computation and tax assessment is available; for a non-resident owned AG, ownership changes do not automatically extinguish loss carryforward unless there is a clear abuse of the loss compensation procedure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing imposes default penalty and procedural fines typically up to CHF 10,000 per canton; default interest of about 4.5% per annum accrues on the assessed tax; repeated failure can trigger an administrative penalty of up to the full tax due and, in serious cases, criminal tax evasion penalties up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax ('Verrechnungssteuer') is levied on distributions of profits and dividends from a Swiss AG.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate on dividends, the shareholder must be the beneficial owner and submit a Swiss Form 823 (or TD DS 04574) together with a valid tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The Swiss payer must obtain the form before payment or the recipient must file a refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid. Traité rates vary by country; exercise domestic anti-abuse conditions including 10% substantive holding and real economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Swiss withholding tax on royalties is 0%. Interest on ordinary commercial loans is generally not subject to Swiss withholding tax, but interest paid on publicly issued bonds and bank deposits may be subject to the 35% statutory rate. Under applicable DTAs, treaty reductions may reduce interest to 0%–10% and royalties to 0%–5% depending on the residence country and creditor's capacity.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss entities of a multinational group with consolidated group revenue of CHF 80 million or more must prepare and submit the Master File. A Local File is required when the Swiss entity's net sales exceed CHF 10 million and intercompany transactions exceed CHF 200,000 per transaction category. For a Helpdesk SaaS AG, the threshold applies to all cross-border intercompany service fees, cost recharges, and IP royalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply a formal 'Economic Substance Regulations' (ESR) regime akin to onshore tax havens, but the Federal Tax Administration enforces substance-over-form and OECD BEPS principles. A Helpdesk AG must demonstrate sufficient board governance, local employees with decision-making authority, physical premises (or appropriate home-office arrangements), and actual performance of core income-generating activities. A letterbox company without substance may lose treaty benefits, trigger legal rewrites of revenue, and face harsher penalties under tax evasion and money laundering statutes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG claims treaty reduction on dividends paid to a non-resident shareholder without proving beneficial ownership, lifetime dividend distribution disguised as loans, or offshore shell structures artificially transferring SaaS revenues to a tax-haven entity with no operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax (DBG) and Substantive Tax Law impose an administrative fine equal to the evaded tax, plus a penal surcharge up to three times the evaded amount. Unpaid withholding tax is recoverable with default interest of 4.5% per annum; the Swiss tax authority can render the foreign recipient jointly liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for deliberate or grossly negligent tax underpayments; Swiss board members face criminal imprisonment up to three years or civil restitution of withheld taxes, and under the Federal Criminal Act, can be subject to travel bans and repatriation of funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG has no physical office in Switzerland, no resident director, uses the helpdesk software and customer support staff in a zero- or low-tax jurisdiction, and passes over 90% of profit as intercompany fees without any local operating person's decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA may disregard the AG's tax residence, attribute the profit to the economic owner abroad, or apply the 'direct offset' rule. Penalties include denial of treaty benefits, an assessment at the higher federal effective rate plus cantonal penalties, and legal voidance of the AG's corporate existence if actual commercial activity has ceased.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and beneficial owners who orchestrate a sham vehicle face administrative fines of up to CHF 500,000, criminal confiscation orders, and potential extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties for tax fraud offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG processes prepaid subscriptions and payouts through US-based payment rails without conducting Know-Your-Client (KYC), does not maintain accurate beneficiary registers, or allows customers to load funds anonymously from non-Swiss bank accounts and withdraw as cash-like refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) applies to financial intermediaries; if the helpdesk platform begins to hold client funds, a FINMA license might be required. Sanctions reach a fine of up to CHF 500,000 for institutions and CHF 100,000 for individuals, plus withdrawal of the operating licence and asset freezing orders by the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be criminally liable for failing to report suspicious activity; severe cases trigger imprisonment of up to three years. Civil liability requires restitution of laundered assets, and international cooperation measures can impose travel bans and seizure of personal bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG files a Swiss corporate return reporting zero taxable profit while economically receiving a full margin under a bogus cost-plus arrangement; the foreign parent transfers IP and helpdesk software royalties at a premium to a low-tax jurisdiction, creating a mismatch that triggers OECD BEPS countermeasures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss courts may apply the 'substance-over-form' doctrine to recompute the taxable profit at the full arm's length value; interest on the adjustment at 4.5% per year, plus a penalty of up to 30% of the extra assessed tax. Under the OECD Multilateral Instrument, treaty benefits for abusive structures are denied retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations or endorse fraudulent transfer pricing reports face criminal proceedings for forgery, imprisonment up to five years, personal liability for civil damages to minority shareholders, and a ban from serving as board members of any Swiss corporation for up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG pays a dividend to its sole US parent company without deducting the statutory 35% Swiss withholding tax on the full amount, and does not obtain a reduced-rate pre-clearance under the US-Switzerland DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Federal Withholding Tax Act (VStG), the unpaid withholding tax is a priority claim against the AG; the FTA can impose a penalty equal to 5% of the gross dividend for each commenced month of non-collection, plus interest and a late-payment surcharge of up to 150% of the statutory tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors become personally and jointly liable for the uncollected withholding tax if they knowingly failed to register as tax-exempt or omitted to deduct; Swiss law also allows forced liquidation and a personal ban on leaving the country until the outstanding tax debt is settled.
